newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia police accuse two more of German kidnap.
newsitem.headline: Colombia police accuse two more of German kidnap.

text.p: Two suspected leftist rebels were arrested early on Saturday in northwest Colombia on charges of kidnapping a German woman who was freed under mysterious circumstances in mid-November, police said.

Brigitte Schoene, the wife of a former BASF Chemicals executive, was allegedly snatched by National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels from her home near the northwestern city of Medellin in mid-August. She was freed on Nov. 17 when anti-kidnap police arrested a shadowy German private eye, Werner Mauss, and his wife Michaela as they tried to bundle her on board a private charter plane bound for Venezuela.

A total of seven suspected ELN members have now been arrested on charges of abducting Schoene. Mauss and his wife have also been charged with aggravated kidnap, but the full extent of their links with the ELN or how they came to be holding Schoene is still not fully clear.
Colombian officials insist Mauss is an international head of the ELN. The German authorities say Mauss was in Colombia on a "humanitarian" rescue mission.
Prison authorities meanwhile searched Mauss' cell in the high-security jail of Itagui near Medellin on Friday, prison officials said. No illicit property was found.
